title: LLM orchestration onramp - Sparrow Systems discovery
summary: Introductory discovery to map Sparrow Systems' needs for hosted vs dedicated vs private Redwood deployments. Discussed SDK integration patterns (LangChain, LlamaIndex), proxy/gateway sidecar approach, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks, and security/compliance requirements. Agreed to run a proof-of-concept (small bench) against their evaluation dataset and share security docs and pricing tiers.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
SDKs and orchestration with LangChain / LlamaIndex
Rate limits, quotas, burst handling and fallback policies
Observability: token-level cost, traces, per-model dashboards
Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs, data residency
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + security pack and KMS integration notes (Maya)
Schedule bench run with Sparrow's eval set (Jordan to coordinate, target week of Jan 19)
Share SDK quickstart + LangChain example repo (Maya)
Intro to Redwood Dedicated sales engineer for capacity planning (Samir)
Follow-up call to review bench results and latency/cost tradeoffs (2 weeks)
action_items: Maya Chen: Email SOC2/security docs and customer-specific KMS checklist (due: 2026-01-12)
Jordan Reed: Prepare benchmark template and test steps; coordinate access (due: 2026-01-16)
Priya Nair: Provide sample traffic profile and SLO targets (due: 2026-01-13)
Lena Ortiz: Confirm stakeholders for procurement and legal (due: 2026-01-14)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got the team from Sparrow, appreciate you making time. I can see Lena, Marcus, Priya, Tom and Evan. quick intros?
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: yeah thanks maya, im lena, cto at Sparrow Systems. we run internal search and agent orchestration for customer support. main thing for today is to figure out how Redwood would sit in our stack, and whether hosted is safe or we need private.
[00:28] Marcus Hale: hi all, marcus - principal ml eng. i'll be leading the eval and care about latency and model consistency with our prompt templates.
[00:36] Priya Nair: priya, infra. curious about network patterns, gateway, sidecars, and how much we have to change in our edge services.
[00:44] Tom Benson: tom, security. i'll ask the SOC2/KMS/SSO questions.
[00:48] Maya Chen: great. quick overview from our side: i'm maya, your AE; jordan reed is our solutions engineer and he'll go deeper into infra and perf. Jordan?
[00:56] Jordan Reed: hey, thanks. shameless plug: we optimize for predictable inference—so things like batching, kv cache, and routing policies are first-class. we'll walk through integration patterns and what the effort looks like.
[01:08] Evan Liu: quick Q up front—are there client-side SDKs that play nicely with LangChain and LlamaIndex? we have a small agent orchestration layer built on top of langchain.
[01:16] Jordan Reed: yes — we have official SDKs in Python/Node, and published examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. the key is whether you want to call Redwood directly from the orchestration layer or put a gateway/sidecar in front.
[01:28] Marcus Hale: what's the tradeoff? latency vs control?
[01:31] Jordan Reed: exact tradeoffs. direct SDK calls mean lower network hops and easier token-level tracing. gateway or proxy lets you centralize auth, rate limiting, and shapings—good when you need cross-team policy. sidecar gives you local caching for KV and prefix cache, so you can reduce repetitive token generation cost.
[01:47] Priya Nair: do you have a recommended pattern for a multi-region app? we've got EU and US infra, data residency constraints sometimes.
[01:55] Jordan Reed: we recommend Smart Routing — route requests by policy (region, latency, data residency). Hosted supports region pinning; Dedicated/Dedicated-in-VPC gives you more control if you need strict residency. for hybrid, a private control plane with customer-managed networking is an option.
[02:12] Lena Ortiz: security Q—what's in the SOC2 pack, and do you integrate with our KMS?
[02:18] Maya Chen: we'll send the SOC2 and security pack after the call. in short: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations for dedicated/private. for hosted we offer encryption-in-transit and at-rest; for HSM/KMS you should consider Dedicated/Private.
[02:33] Tom Benson: any customer that's had to go fully air-gapped on-prem?
[02:36] Jordan Reed: yes, we've done on-prem packages for regulated customers. that path has longer lead times—think weeks to months—and requires coordination on hardware, but it's doable.
[02:46] Evan Liu: about rate limits—how granular are quotas? per-API-key, per-route? do you support burst policies?
[02:51] Jordan Reed: we support per-token and per-route quotas; per-key throttles, and a burst bucket. plus automatic fallback policies: e.g., route to a cheaper quantized variant or degrade to shorter responses. you can also configure per-customer SLAs with Dedicated.
[03:07] Marcus Hale: what's the mechanism for fallback—does that require app logic or is it automatic?
[03:11] Jordan Reed: can be either. Redwood's routing engine can automatically fallback to compatible model variants or different capacity tiers based on policy. apps can also observe error codes and invoke alternate flows.
[03:21] Lena Ortiz: ok. integration: we use LangChain agents that swap models dynamically. can we keep the same API surface so we don't have to rewrite a lot?
[03:30] Maya Chen: yes. SDKs mirror the API you'd expect—text/generate, chat streams, embeddings. our sample LangChain connectors show minimal changes. Jordan, show the example?
[03:38] Jordan Reed: sure — (brief pause) here's a rough snippet: client = RedwoodClient(...); lc = LangChainClient(client) — exchange is small: you pass the same prompt template, and the SDK handles kv cache support and streaming tokens. note: sometimes transcribed examples show mis-typed method names in older SDK versions, so check the latest repo.
[03:57] Marcus Hale: if we use LlamaIndex as our retrieval layer, any gotchas?
[04:01] Jordan Reed: LlamaIndex connectors are straightforward; main gotcha is tokenization mismatch on embedding models—ensure your retrieval encoder matches Redwood embeddings model variant. also watch out for batch sizes during re-ranking.
[04:13] Priya Nair: about the gateway—we prefer a lightweight sidecar per service vs a centralized gateway for performance. does Redwood support sidecar-based observability hooks?
[04:22] Jordan Reed: yes — sidecars can emit tracing spans and token-level cost to your observability backend. we provide OpenTelemetry-compatible hooks and per-request metadata to correlate traces. centralized gateway easier for policy, sidecar better for low-latency metrics.
[04:36] Tom Benson: audit log retention and search—how deep does Redwood go?
[04:40] Maya Chen: hosted includes audit logs with retention tiers; Dedicated/Private gives you longer retention and S3 export or SIEM integration. we'll include retention tables in the security pack.
[04:51] Evan Liu: bench questions — what metrics should we collect in our POC?
[04:55] Jordan Reed: latency p50/p95, token cost per request, concurrency throughput, error rates, tail latencies with batching, and quality metrics vs your prompt eval set. we'll provide a benchmark template.
[05:08] Marcus Hale: re: quantization — do you have recommended quantized variants for cost savings, and how do model quality regressions surface?
[05:15] Jordan Reed: yes, we maintain model profiles showing perf vs quality. our Optimize tooling flags regressions against your eval prompts and can gate rollout. quantized models are generally fine for many tasks but we recommend testing on a subset first.
[05:29] Lena Ortiz: curious about KV cache—if we run multi-turn agents across sessions, can the caching be externalized?
[05:36] Jordan Reed: KV cache is stored at the serving layer—can be pinned to a session or externalized to a cache layer we coordinate with (Redis-backed store) for long-term persistence. sidecar patterns help here too.
[05:49] Priya Nair: network architecture—if we go Dedicated in a VPC, does Redwood put anything in customer VPC? how's the control plane handled?
[05:57] Jordan Reed: for Private/VPC deployments, the control plane can be customer-managed. compute sits in your VPC under dedicated pools; we can integrate with your KMS and IAM. for Dedicated reserved capacity we handle runtime but can peer with your networks for egress.
[06:12] Tom Benson: SSO—do you support SAML and provisioning?
[06:15] Maya Chen: yes. SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning for users, RBAC config—these are standard enterprise features.
[06:22] Marcus Hale: latency SLOs—what's realistic for p95 with a 2k token generation?
[06:28] Jordan Reed: depends on model and hardware. for hosted small LLMs p95 might be 300-600ms; larger models or longer tokens push to multiple seconds. with Dedicated and pinned GPUs you can get more predictable p95s. batching and KV cache affect this a lot.
[06:42] Evan Liu: cost modeling—do you provide token-level cost breakdown per route?
[06:46] Maya Chen: yes, Console shows token-level cost, per-route and per-model. you can export cost breakdowns per time window.
[06:52] Lena Ortiz: procurement—what's the minimally viable contract if we wanted to start a pilot?
[06:56] Maya Chen: for pilots we usually do a short eval agreement with a small committed monthly spend and the hosted API. if you need consistent throughput we propose a short dedicated pilot with reserved capacity. legal usually starts once you hit enterprise thresholds.
[07:10] Marcus Hale: we need to test throughput under our peak: 200 concurrent agent sessions, avg 400 tokens each. Priya can share exact traffic profile.
[07:19] Priya Nair: yes i'll share the traffic spreadsheet. we also need to know about autoscaling and burst behavior if we go dedicated.
[07:26] Jordan Reed: autoscaling policies for Dedicated: configurable min/max pools, burst to shared capacity, and graceful degradation policies. we'll work with you on config to meet SLOs.
[07:36] Tom Benson: do you support customer-managed keys in hosted at all? or only in Dedicated/Private?
[07:41] Maya Chen: customer-managed keys for encryption at rest are available on Dedicated/Private. hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default.
[07:48] Evan Liu: any SDK gotchas for streaming responses with LangChain agents?
[07:52] Jordan Reed: streaming is supported; common gotcha is handling partial tokens and reconciling with agent step logic. we have sample code that handles token chunking and finalization hooks. also watch for out-of-order events in noisy networks.
[08:05] Lena Ortiz: sample timeline—how long for a Dedicated pilot?
[08:09] Samir Kapoor: typical onboarding for Dedicated pilot is 2-4 weeks for provisioning and basic tests, 4-8 weeks for full capacity and security review depending on procurement.
[08:20] Marcus Hale: for the bench, what access do you need? API key? VPC peering?
[08:24] Jordan Reed: for a hosted bench we just need API key and sample payloads. for a Dedicated bench we'll request a temporary peering and network access or run synthetic traffic from our test harness against your endpoints.
[08:36] Priya Nair: we likely start with hosted eval then move to Dedicated if throughput is a problem.
[08:40] Maya Chen: that's a common path. we'll aim to make hosted feel production-like for your eval and then help with migration.
[08:46] Evan Liu: any specific compliance flags—EU data residency?
[08:49] Maya Chen: we have region pinning on hosted but for strict residency Dedicated/Private is recommended. we'll include region docs in the pack.
[08:58] Lena Ortiz: okay great. can you include an example of a gateway sidecar config and a LangChain connector?
[09:02] Jordan Reed: yep we'll put examples in the repo. note: examples sometimes show older endpoints; that's why we keep a versioned set of examples.
[09:12] (crosstalk)
[09:14] Marcus Hale: one more — observability export—do you support raw token traces to our datadog/newrelic?
[09:19] Jordan Reed: yes — via OpenTelemetry or direct export. you can correlate tokens to traces and to cost. we don't export PII by default; logs can be redacted.
[09:29] Tom Benson: redaction is key. do you offer PII detection or masking?
[09:33] Jordan Reed: we have optional PII detection in the pipeline and curated redaction hooks you can insert. we'll include details in the security pack.
[09:41] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. what's next?
[09:43] Maya Chen: recap — we'll send security docs, share SDK + LangChain examples, Jordan will prepare a benchmark template, Priya to share traffic, and we'll schedule a bench the week of Jan 19.
[09:55] Lena Ortiz: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:57] Marcus Hale: thanks everyone.
[09:59] Maya Chen: we'll follow up via email with links and a calendar invite. have a good afternoon all.
[10:04] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attributed lines and truncated method names; filler words preserved; some technical terms spelled inexactly (e.g., 'kv cache' sometimes 'k v cache'), proper nouns sometimes capitalized inconsistently.
